logline: A near-perfect student discovers his elite high school runs on ruthless social Darwinism - and that the real curriculum is learning to manipulate everyone around you.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb places it at 7.7 across the series; Season 1 earns its place as a sharp psychological setup with a slow-burn payoff, though viewers and critics noted its deliberately opaque protagonist and uneven pacing mid-season.

pull_quotes.text: A surprisingly sharp psychological thriller wrapped in a high school setting - the cold logic of its protagonist is genuinely unsettling.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 of Classroom of the Elite debuted in summer 2017 to a split reception: admirers praised studio Lerche's clinical, Kubrickian framing of Kiyotaka Ayanokoji as anime's most deliberately unknowable protagonist, while detractors flagged slow mid-season pacing and character arcs left frustratingly incomplete. The premise - a meritocratic school where Class D's outcasts scheme to climb the system - drew comparisons to Kakegurui and Death Note for its pleasure in watching calculated manipulation. IMDb audiences settled around 7.7, reflecting genuine enthusiasm tempered by the adaptation's compressed light novel plotting. Critics at Diabolical Plots and THEM Anime Reviews found the psychological layer compelling even when the execution stumbled, noting the finale recontextualises everything the season spent twelve episodes pretending to be.

episode_reviews.title: Do the Inferior Deserve Salvation?
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces Class D's deliberately mediocre placement in a school that promises equality but runs on hidden hierarchy. Ayanokoji's first-episode detachment reads as blankness until the final scene recasts it as something more calculated.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The closing shot reframes everything the premiere spent 24 minutes presenting as background noise.

episode_reviews.title: The Survival of the Fittest
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale's island arc crystallises what the show has been building toward - Ayanokoji's capacity for cold, total strategy finally made explicit. The show's slow-burn pays off in its most audacious single scene.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Ayanokoji's island revelation - the moment fan communities spent years dissecting.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 raised the MAL score trajectory to approximately 8.1, with fans crediting deeper Class D rivalry arcs and a more confident directorial hand from Lerche after the five-year gap.

seasons.review_body: Five years after Season 1's cliffhanger, Season 2 arrived in July 2022 and immediately satisfied the fanbase that had consumed the light novels in the interim. Lerche doubled down on the series' cold intelligence - extended classroom showdowns, layered class rivalries, and Ayanokoji's escalating shadow plays rewarded patient viewers. MAL community ratings climbed relative to Season 1, reflecting the adaptation's improved confidence in trusting audience investment. The season's thirteen episodes prioritised cumulative payoff over episodic accessibility, which divided newer viewers but cemented the franchise's standing among psychological anime aficionados. The series' Anime-Planet page accumulated reviews citing Season 2 as the point the adaptation stopped feeling provisional.
seasons.season_over_season: A substantial improvement over Season 1 - the five-year gap allowed Lerche to sharpen the adaptation, and the deeper character rivalries made the psychological games feel genuinely consequential rather than merely clever.

bollymeter.basis: MAL community tracking placed Season 3 at approximately 8.34, representing the series' peak critical standing; fans cited escalating Ayanokoji reveals and the season's willingness to resolve long-building arcs.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 (January-March 2024) is the franchise's high-water mark by audience consensus. MAL community ratings reached approximately 8.34, and the season's structural confidence drew comparisons on Anime-Planet to Hyouka and The Promised Neverland at their peaks - fewer detours, tighter rivalry mechanics, a climax the adaptation had been building toward across three seasons. LiveChart tracking confirmed 434,000 scorers for this season, a significant expansion in the Western fanbase. Lerche's willingness to commit to Ayanokoji's moral grey areas rather than softening them for mainstream appeal is the distinguishing creative choice. Season 4 following in April 2026 confirms continued production confidence.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 is the clearest indication the adaptation has found its rhythm - the psychological set-pieces land harder because three seasons of investment are now in play.

bollymeter.basis: Early MAL tracking placed Season 4 at 8.29 after its April 2026 premiere, consistent with Season 3's ceiling; verdict open while the season is still airing.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 premiered April 1, 2026, with MAL early-episode ratings tracking at 8.29 - consistent with the franchise's established ceiling per Anime Rave's social tracking (April 2026). The adaptation continues Lerche's confident handling of Shogo Kinugasa's source material. As of June 2026, the season is still airing; full critical and audience verdicts remain open. Early MAL trajectory suggests the rivalry mechanics continue at Season 3's elevated level rather than declining into the franchise-fatigue pattern common in long-running anime adaptations.
seasons.season_over_season: Early tracking suggests Season 4 maintains the quality ceiling Season 3 established rather than declining - a notable achievement for a fourth run.
